answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The raven multiplier is published, charged in delta, and relic lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 3812 identities would post 4940 proofs and burn roughly 66 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
